S105.01.needs: a paid account with API access (other plans get no keys)
S105.01.note: Organizations are not created in this panel: a workspace is created in Settings > Workspace under 'Create your workspace' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/TeamSection.tsx). Projects belong to the active workspace.
steps: Open /developers in the browser or the Desktop app.
Click New project in the Projects card.
Type Production in Name and 500 in Monthly limit in credits, then click Create project.
Look at the Projects list: the new project appears, with a spend line that ends in 'this month' and shows the limit you typed (or 'no monthly limit' if blank).
S105.01.where: Type /developers after the site address (no menu link found) > Projects > New project

S105.02.needs: a plan with API access (other plans see an upgrade message instead of the form)
S105.02.note: The screen says Delete, not Revoke. The same card also appears on /developers.
steps: Click the account menu (labelled Account menu for your name), click Settings, then Account, then the API keys row.
Click New Key. Type a name, pick a project or keep Default project, choose Expires (Never, 30 days, 90 days or 1 year), and tick scopes (Read model catalog, Run inference, Read usage).
Click Generate Key, then Copy to Clipboard. The full key is shown only once.
Check the list: each key shows its prefix followed by '...', Created, Last used once used, and Expires or Never expires.
Click the trash icon labelled Delete <name>, then Delete Key, and check the key is gone from the list.
S105.02.where: Settings > Account > API keys > New Key

S105.03.needs: a workspace owner or admin on a Team or Enterprise plan (the create form shows only for accounts that can manage keys)
S105.03.note: The service principals panel has no create button; a principal is created with the first workspace API key. Principals can be disabled or enabled but not revoked there; revoke is on workspace keys.
steps: Open Settings, click Workspace, then Workspace administration.
Click Audit, scroll to Workspace API keys, type a name, pick an expiry, tick at least one scope and click Create key. Copy the key shown.
Click Identity and scroll to Service principals. Find the principal the key created.
Click Disable on a principal and check it now says Disabled and its button reads Enable.
Back on Audit, click Revoke on a workspace key, confirm Revoke key, and check the key shows Revoked.
S105.03.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Audit (Workspace API keys) and Identity (Service principals)

S105.04.note: The catalogue lists models the account's plan can reach. No filter for what one specific API key can call was found.
steps: Open /developers and scroll to the Reference card.
Click Models. Check the page heading reads Models and a list of model cards appears.
Open a model card and read its Context line and its capability chips.
Click the Plan access filter 'In your plan' and check which models remain.

S105.12.needs: a signed-in account (commands sync to the account)
S105.12.note: A command has one input slot ({{input}} in the template), not named arguments. The Prompts and evaluations card on /developers is a separate versioned-prompt feature.
steps: Open Settings, click General, and scroll to Custom commands.
Click New command. Type a Name (lower case, no spaces), a Description, and a Template that contains the input token.
Click Create command and check it appears in the list.
Click into the chat box, type / and the command name, add some text and send.
Check the reply follows the template with your text in place of the input token.
S105.12.where: Settings > General > Custom commands > New command

S105.18.needs: a paid plan (the history section is hidden on the Free plan)
S105.18.note: Usage is shown in credits. Cost in money is not shown on this screen.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went and choose Days, Weeks or Months.
Read the tables By product area, By model and By project for the chosen period.
Compare: the By model table lists each model with its usage over time.
S105.18.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went

S105.19.needs: an AGI API key and any HTTP client, to see the per-response headers
S105.19.note: The card shows the static limits only. The remaining count is in response headers, not on the page.
steps: Open /developers and scroll to the Rate limits card.
Read the list 'Request limits by endpoint': each row gives an endpoint, a number of requests per window, and whether it counts per account or per IP for an API key.
Read the card text: each response carries X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset.
Send a request with an AGI API key and read those headers to see how close you are to the limit. Compare with Expected.

S105.20.needs: a workspace owner or admin account for the workspace cap; a paid plan for the personal cap
S105.20.note: The enforcement choices are Off, Notify and Block. Whether the API refuses calls at the cap was not checked here.
steps: Open Settings, click Workspace, then Workspace administration, then Usage.
Scroll to Monthly spend limit. Type an amount, set Spend limit enforcement to Block, and click Set limit.
Check the card shows the cap you set and the enforcement choice.
For a personal cap, open Settings > Usage and find Monthly spend limit; set and check it the same way.
S105.20.where: Settings > Workspace > Workspace administration > Usage (Monthly spend limit); personal cap at Settings > Usage > Monthly spend limit

S105.21.needs: a paid account with API access, and an HTTPS address you control to receive events
steps: Open /developers, scroll to the Webhooks card and click Add endpoint.
Type an https address in Endpoint URL and optionally a Description.
Under Events, tick the events you want to receive.
Click Add endpoint and read the Copy the signing secret now dialog.
Check the new endpoint appears in the Webhook endpoints list.

S105.22.needs: a registered endpoint that can receive HTTPS requests
steps: Open /developers, scroll to Webhooks, and make sure an endpoint is listed.
Click Send test event on the endpoint, or use an event that already happened.
Click Deliveries on the endpoint row and read Recent deliveries: each row shows a status such as Delivered, Failed or Retrying after N attempts.
Click Resend on a delivery row and check its status updates.
S105.22.where: Developer console (/developers) > Webhooks > endpoint row > Deliveries

S105.23.note: The page states there is no AGI SDK, so the 'official client SDK' Expected is met only by OpenAI's libraries.
steps: Open the API docs page (type /api-docs after the site address, or use the API entry in the site menu).
Scroll to the section titled SDKs.
Read it: it says there is no AGI SDK and that OpenAI's official libraries are the client.
Look at the Python and TypeScript tabs under it and check they show example code for the gateway.
Compare with Expected: the docs cover OpenAI's libraries, not a separate AGI SDK.
Open the API docs page and scroll to the section titled Reference.
Read the paragraph: the OpenAPI bundle describes every endpoint and the credential each one takes.
Click OpenAPI bundle and check a JSON document opens.
Scroll to the top, click Authentication and scopes, and read which credential each endpoint accepts.
S105.24.where: API docs page > Reference. > OpenAPI bundle

S105.25.note: Whether the samples have a copy button was not checked.
steps: Open the API docs page. The first example sits under the title 'One chat completion against the gateway'.
Click the tabs curl, Python and TypeScript in turn and read each sample.
Scroll to SDKs. and click the Python and TypeScript tabs there.
Compare with Expected: each tab shows a copyable request to the gateway.
S105.25.where: API docs page > code tabs curl, Python, TypeScript

steps: Open the API docs page and scroll to Moving to the gateway.
Read the three sub-headings: From the OpenAI API, From the Anthropic API and Between models.
Open the text under From the Anthropic API and read the steps to change the client.
Compare with Expected: there is a guide for each other provider and one for moving between models.
S105.26.where: API docs page > Moving to the gateway. > From the OpenAI API / From the Anthropic API / Between models

S105.27.note: No retirement is scheduled today, so the table is not visible unless one is added.
steps: Open the API docs page and scroll to Deprecations.
Read the text: each model carries a deprecation date, which is empty until a retirement is scheduled.
Read the table Scheduled model retirements if it appears; otherwise the page says No model retirements are scheduled.
Open /developers > Reference > Models and look for a model marked Retiring with a date.
Compare with Expected: retirements appear in advance with a date.
S105.27.where: API docs page > Deprecations. ; model cards on Developer console > Reference > Models

steps: Open Settings and click Help.
Click Contact support to open the support page and read the Raise a ticket button there.
Back in Help, scroll to Your support tickets and fill in Subject and What happened.
Click Raise ticket and check the new ticket appears in the list with its Raised date and priority.
S105.28.where: Settings > Help > Contact support, then Settings > Help > Your support tickets > Raise ticket

S105.29.needs: a plugin .zip file with a skills folder (a manifest folder is optional)
S105.29.note: Create a plugin is the other option in the Add menu. Both appear only when the directory offers them to this account.
steps: Open Settings and click Plugins.
Click Add, then Upload plugin.
Choose a .zip of a plugin that has a skills folder, and submit the dialog.
Check the plugin shows under Installed and can be opened.

S105.30.needs: a plugin you created; an admin must approve it in the plugin moderation page before it is listed
S105.30.note: Approval happens in the admin plugin moderation page, outside this tester path. A new version of an approved plugin uses Submit this version.
steps: Open Settings, click Plugins, and open a plugin you created.
Click Submit to the directory.
Read the confirmation text and click Submit for review.
Check the plugin shows a pending submission with a Withdraw action.
S105.30.where: Settings > Plugins > open your plugin > Submit to the directory
